blocks.heading: Questions 11-12
blocks.title: Riverside Community Garden — Volunteer Notice
paragraphs: Riverside Community Garden welcomes new volunteers this spring.
The garden is open for volunteering on Saturdays, from nine in the morning until one in the afternoon.
Volunteers plant vegetables, water the raised beds and repair the wooden fence along the river path.
No experience is required. Tools and gloves are provided at the shed beside the gate.
Please wear closed shoes, because the soil near the beds stays wet until noon.
Sign up at the front desk one week before the Saturday you choose, so that the staff can order enough seedlings.
Members who volunteer three times receive a free packet of seeds for their own garden.

blocks.heading: Questions 13-15
blocks.title: Why Cities Are Planting Trees Again
paragraphs: For most of the twentieth century, city planners treated trees as decoration. Streets were widened for cars, and the shade that had once cooled the pavement disappeared. Only in the last two decades have engineers begun to describe a street tree as a piece of equipment with a measurable function.

The job is mainly cooling. A mature tree moves water from the soil into the air, and that process removes heat in the same way that sweat cools skin. Measurements in several European cities show that a shaded street can be four degrees cooler than a similar street nearby without trees. The difference matters most on summer nights, when heat stored in concrete keeps flats warm long after sunset. Similar results appear in a survey of North American cities.

Trees also slow rainfall. Leaves hold part of a storm and release it gradually, so less water reaches the drains at once. Councils that once paid to enlarge underground pipes now find that planting is cheaper. The catch is patience: a young tree gives little shade, and the benefit that pays for the work arrives twenty years later, usually after the council that planted it has left office.

blocks.heading: Questions 26-30
blocks.title: Measuring Noise in a Reading Room
paragraphs: Every university library faces the same complaint: the reading room is too noisy. Until recently the only evidence was the complaint itself, which told the staff nothing about when the noise happened or where it came from.

[A] In 2019 a library in Manchester attached small sound meters to eight shelves. [B] The method was deliberately simple: the meters recorded loudness once a minute for a full term, and no recording of speech was kept, so nobody could be identified from the data.

[C] The result surprised the staff. The loudest hour was not the evening, when the room was full, but the middle of the morning, when it was half empty. [D] Groups arriving together talked in the aisles before they sat down.

Two changes followed. The entrance was moved to the far end of the room, so that arriving groups no longer walked past the desks, and a small discussion area was opened next door. Noise in the reading room then dropped by about a quarter.

The research is often quoted as proof that measurement beats guessing. That is fair, but the meters answered only the question they were asked. They could not say whether students left the library because of the noise, and nobody counted them.

targetSkills: Scanning a public notice for one required instruction
Following a cause-and-effect explanation across paragraphs
Choosing the word that fits a grammatical slot

teaching.objective: Read a short public notice and an explanatory passage for detail, and say why the writer includes a particular fact.
strategy: Read the question stem before the passage, then look only for the sentence that answers it.
In a cloze, decide the part of speech first; the hint letters confirm the word, they do not choose it.
For a why-does-the-writer question, look at the sentence before and after the detail, not at the detail itself.
commonErrors: Choosing a word that matches the hint letters but not the grammar of the sentence.
Answering a detail question from memory of the topic instead of from the passage.
Treating an example as the writer's main point.
